reasons: **It gets most of the job done, but heat is very tight.** This plan finishes about three-quarters of the most important work. Even the hottest workers should stay just under the safe body-heat limit, by less than two-tenths of a degree. There's almost no room for extra effort or a hotter-than-expected day, so watch your crew closely and enforce breaks.
**Everyone comes inside from 2:00 to 3:00 p.m.** Lightning is expected then, so no outdoor work during that hour. That lost time is part of why not all the work fits in today.

**Other options trade work for heat.** A plan that spreads the work more evenly across the crew gets the same amount done with the same heat level. A plan that front-loads the heavy work before 10:00 a.m. keeps people slightly cooler but gets a bit less done (about 71% instead of 75%). If the day feels hotter than forecast, switching to the early heavy-work plan is the safer choice.

Hard safety rules:
- Every worker's 90th percentile core temperature must stay below 38.0 °C all shift. Harder work, sun and high WBGT heat people up; 30-min shade rests cool them down.
- Breaks: at most 3 work slots in a row, then a 'rest' slot; at most 2 in a row if any of those slots has WBGT >= 30.0 °C.
- No outdoor tasks during hazards that stop outdoor work. After lightning, outdoor work stays stopped for 30 more minutes.
- Workers who are not acclimatized never do very_heavy tasks when WBGT >= 28.0 °C.
Validity: one entry per slot per worker; off-site workers rest; skills and allowed slots must match.
